source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3 (nominations for county and rural councils: the Ballymena rural district list)
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Unopposed returns read on the page image of the Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3 (the Ballymena rural district list: 'Unopposed returns are:-', 21 divisions, the name as filed); the Northern Whig's 'Rural council nominations' of the same day (p. 3), cited before, has no Ballymena list.

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 3 October 1946. Two divisions were contested; the remaining twenty-one were filled unopposed at the nominations of 19 September. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected (council-audit, Nov 2026): 'M'Mastcr' is an OCR misreading of M'Master ('cr' for 'er'); not read on the image, as the cited article's image does not show the Ballymena list. Corrected from the page image of the Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the unopposed return is now cited to the page that prints it (was the Northern Whig, 20 September 1946, p. 3, whose rural nominations list omits Ballymena); the name is unchanged. Renamed from 'Cloughogue' to Cloghogue (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Ballymena Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Cloghogue; the rounds were filed as Cloughogue (1924, 1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1961); Cloghogue (1952, 1955, 1958, 1964, 1967). This round was filed as 'Cloughogue', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (cloughogue) answers with a redirect to this one.
